sar.narrative: This Suspicious Activity Report details unauthorized card-not-present transactions involving customer C03237 and card account C03237-K1. Between November 7, 2016, and November 10, 2016, two unauthorized online transactions totaling $199.89 were processed in billing region 264. The initial unauthorized transaction 3438063 was executed on November 7, 2016, for $99.95 utilizing a newly observed device, D006648. On November 10, 2016, a second unauthorized charge of $99.94 (transaction 3445840) was conducted using device D003615, identified as an iOS Device running iOS 11.2.5 on mobile Safari. The bank's fraud monitoring model scored transaction 3445840 at 0.991, whereas legitimate customer activity occurred in billing region 272 from device D006776 with scores below 0.005. Both fraudulent transactions shared holder identity C03237-K1|264|113, which was established as compromised in historical fraud case CC-5231. Furthermore, device D003615 is tied to twelve historical fraud cases and was concurrently observed across four additional high-risk card accounts (C04661-K1, C06147-K2, C06374-K1, and C09530-K1) during the same weekly window. The recurrence of identical unauthorized amounts, compromised holder credentials, and shared device infrastructure across cards indicate coordinated card-not-present fraud. Card C03237-K1 has been blocked, connected accounts have been flagged for monitoring, and this report is submitted accordingly.

passages.section: Section 3a. A case is not a report
passages.text: Section 3a. A case is not a report. Two different things, and the agent produces both. **A case** (`CREATE_CASE`) is the bank's internal record of an investigation. Open one whenever fraud probability reaches 0.30, whenever you request evidence, or whenever a customer disputes a charge. A case can be closed as fraud or as legitimate. It can be updated when new evidence arrives. It should be written into the graph so later investigations can find it: a case that names a merchant or a device becomes evidence for the next analyst. **A suspicious activity report** (`FILE_REPORT`) is a regulatory filing sent outside the bank. File one when fraud is confirmed or strongly suspected **and** at least one of these holds: exposure exceeds $1,000; the activity connects to a shared device profile, a shared region cluster, or another customer's fraud; the pattern is coordinated or undocumented (rule R9). A report always has a case behind it. Most cases never need a report. The report narrative must stand on its own: who, what, when, where, how, and why it is suspicious. Deciding correctly between ""case only"" and ""case plus report"" is part of the next-best-action score.

Rule R6: Shared origin. When several cards show fraud from the same device profile, the same billing region, or the same recipient email in one window, name the shared element, recommend `CREATE_CASE` and `FILE_REPORT`, and `MONITOR_CONNECTED_CARDS` for every card that shares it.

report.sar_narrative: This Suspicious Activity Report details unauthorized card-not-present transactions involving customer C03237 and card account C03237-K1. Between November 7, 2016, and November 10, 2016, two unauthorized online transactions totaling $199.89 were processed in billing region 264. The initial unauthorized transaction 3438063 was executed on November 7, 2016, for $99.95 utilizing a newly observed device, D006648. On November 10, 2016, a second unauthorized charge of $99.94 (transaction 3445840) was conducted using device D003615, identified as an iOS Device running iOS 11.2.5 on mobile Safari. The bank's fraud monitoring model scored transaction 3445840 at 0.991, whereas legitimate customer activity occurred in billing region 272 from device D006776 with scores below 0.005. Both fraudulent transactions shared holder identity C03237-K1|264|113, which was established as compromised in historical fraud case CC-5231. Furthermore, device D003615 is tied to twelve historical fraud cases and was concurrently observed across four additional high-risk card accounts (C04661-K1, C06147-K2, C06374-K1, and C09530-K1) during the same weekly window. The recurrence of identical unauthorized amounts, compromised holder credentials, and shared device infrastructure across cards indicate coordinated card-not-present fraud. Card C03237-K1 has been blocked, connected accounts have been flagged for monitoring, and this report is submitted accordingly.
